title: Generating Dicke State Graphs
abstract: Graph theory is a powerful tool in quantum computing, with applications ranging from quantum circuit synthesis and optimization to entanglement mapping. Recent work has shown how one can use edge-colored graphs to model photonic experiments that generate GHZ and W states. However, the latter work also proved that verifying that a graph models a Dicke state experiment is coNP-complete. In this work, we provide families of graphs that generate $|D_{k}^a\rangle \otimes |0\rangle^{\otimes b }$, where $b = |a-2k|$ is the number of spectator modes. The graph setup consists of a doubled complete subgraph on $a$ vertices and a collection of auxiliary vertices. We prove that every coincidence carries exactly $k$ excitations, every weight-$k$ computational basis state on bitstrings of length $a$ is realized, and each of those bitstrings is realized exactly $(n/2)!$ times, where $n = a+b$. Since verifying the Dicke FORALL condition is coNP-complete in general, constructing explicit families that provably generate Dicke states is of interest.
summary: This paper develops graph-theoretic methods to construct photonic quantum circuits that generate specific Dicke states. By analyzing perfect matchings in specially designed graphs, the authors prove that they can reliably generate states of the form $|D_a^kangle \otimes |0angle^{\otimes b}$. This offers a constructive solution to a problem whose general verification is computationally hard.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct explicit families of graphs that provably generate Dicke states, overcoming the computational difficulty of verifying the general Dicke FORALL condition.
main_result: The authors provide a construction using doubled complete subgraphs and auxiliary vertices that guarantees the generation of $|D_a^kangle \otimes |0angle^{\otimes b}$ states, with specific counts for realized bitstrings.
method: The method involves modeling photonic experiments using edge-colored weighted graphs, where the generated state is determined by the superposition of perfect matchings in the graph.
model_or_system: The physical model is photonic quantum experiments simulated by graph theory, where vertices are optical paths and edges represent SPDC crystals. The state generation relies on analyzing the perfect matchings of these graphs.
key_observables: The number of perfect matchings realizing a specific bitstring $\mu(x)$, and the Hamming weight of the resulting excitation pattern.
important_parameters: The parameters include $a$ (signal paths), $k$ (target excitation weight), and $b = |a-2k|$ (spectator modes).
main_assumptions: The construction avoids crystals with an excitation yield of 2 ($ho(e)=2$), and the general verification of the Dicke FORALL condition is coNP-complete.

paper_structure: The paper develops graph theory tools to model quantum state generation, establishes the relationship between perfect matchings and basis states, and culminates in constructing explicit families of graphs that satisfy the Dicke FORALL condition for specific states.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, graph-theoretic blueprints for generating highly entangled states like Dicke states, which are fundamental resources in quantum information processing and quantum optics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: The doubled complete graph on six vertices. Every pair {i, j} carries two parallel edges: one red at i and blue at j, the other red at j and blue at i, for 30 edges in total. Since each edge contributes exactly one red half and a perfect matching has three edges, every matching yields a bitstring of Hamming weight k = 3.

FIG. 2: The graph that generates D5 2 ⊗|0⟩. It consists of a doubled K5 on vertices 1, . . . , 5 in which every pair {i, j} carries two parallel edges, each half red and half blue, such that one edge has red half at i and one edge has red half at j, together with all-blue spokes joining each vertex to vertex 6. This is an example of a sink construction. If the half edges from K5 to 6 were all colored red at i ∈K5 and blue at 6, it would generate D5 3 ⊗|0⟩using a source construction.

FIG. 4: The doubled complete bipartite experiment graph on X = {1, 2, 3} and Y = {4, 5, 6}. Every pair {i, j} with i ∈X, j ∈Y carries two parallel crystals, one emitting |1i, 0j⟩and one emitting |0i, 1j⟩, for 18 crystals in total. Every crystal is excitation-balanced and every coincidence uses three crystals, so every coincidence registers Hamming weight 3.
